Halcyon doesn't have a direct equivalent of a five-business-day postmortem deadline. Its closest rule is a root cause analysis (RCA) that must be completed within **45 calendar days** of the event becoming known, for every Level 1 and Level 2 event [2]. The quality team (QPS) has to charter the RCA team within **72 hours** [2]. Note that 45 calendar days is much longer than your five business days, and the policy I found doesn't set a deadline for an initial written report.

Related timelines that may matter after a serious event:

- **Reporting the event:** Anyone involved or who witnessed it must file a report in SafeReport. The policy says reporting is never optional and never punished [2].
- **Disclosure to the patient or family:** The attending clinician discloses the event, with the charge nurse or medical director present. The policy I found gives no deadline for this [2].
- **Regulatory reporting:** QPS decides whether a state health department or accrediting body must be notified and makes those reports [2]. I found no deadline for these.
- **Privacy incidents:** These are handled separately. Suspected privacy incidents go to the Privacy Officer within 24 hours [3]. Breaches affecting 500 or more people must be reported to HHS within 60 days [3].
- **Review:** Completed RCAs go to the Patient Safety Committee, chaired by the CMO, Dr. Kenji Watanabe, which meets monthly [2].

If you need the exact steps for a sentinel event, check the full sentinel and adverse event reporting policy with QPS.

The knowledge base doesn't use the term "incident commander." The closest equivalent is the **charge nurse**, who coordinates the immediate response to a patient safety event. If no charge nurse is on shift, the **clinic manager** takes that role [2].

- **Who is the charge nurse:** Large clinics always have one. In medium and small clinics, one is designated whenever two or more RNs are on shift. Otherwise, the clinic manager fills the role [1].
- **What the charge nurse does:** After the clinician makes the patient safe and calls 911 if needed, the charge nurse assigns who stays with the patient, who calls the family, and who secures the equipment, medications, or records involved [2].
- **Escalation:** For a sentinel event, the charge nurse notifies the on-call medical director within 1 hour [2]. The on-call director is reached through the answering service at 555-0144, option 2 [3].

The clinic manager is also the escalation point for a site when no charge nurse is on shift [5].

Halcyon's documents require a signed business associate agreement (BAA) before any PHI goes to a vendor. They don't mention a data processing agreement (DPA) anywhere, and the security review requirement is stated for systems and tools rather than as a single vendor-wide gate.

**What's required**

- **Signed BAA before any disclosure.** Under the HIPAA privacy policy, a vendor that will create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on Halcyon's behalf is a business associate, and a signed BAA must be in place before any PHI is disclosed. This applies even to test files or "just a few names" for a pilot [1].
- **Security risk assessment.** New systems that will hold PHI need a security risk assessment, a BAA if a vendor is involved, and an entry in the clinical and business systems inventory before go-live [8]. The HIPAA Security Officer (Ahmed Siddiqui) maintains that inventory [8]. For AI tools, the same list applies, plus a CMIO clinical safety review for clinical use [3].
- **Inventory entry.** The vendor's system must be added to the approved PHI systems list before go-live [8]. The CSCAB chair reminded the board on October 28, 2026 that this must happen before go-live, not after [11].
- **Contact points.** For new tools, email the Privacy Officer (Margaret Holloway) and the HIPAA Security Officer (Ahmed Siddiqui) [3][8].

**Example of the process in practice**

Tallgrass Survey Co. has a completed and passed security risk assessment (September 2026), but its BAA is still unsigned, so no PHI may be shared yet [1]. Quillon Ambient's BAA was executed July 30, 2026, after a risk assessment in July [5].

**What the documents don't cover**

- **DPA:** No source mentions a data processing agreement, its required terms, or whether Halcyon uses one. I can't say whether a DPA is needed in addition to the BAA.
- **Named sign-off for non-AI vendors:** I didn't find a document setting out the approval chain for ordinary (non-AI) vendors. The sources name the Privacy Officer and HIPAA Security Officer as contacts, but not as approvers for every vendor.
- **HIPAA privacy policy text:** I only saw the policy as quoted in vendor records. I did not find the policy itself, so its exact wording on the security review should be checked against the source.

Northwind has an analogous control, but it covers a different kind of access. Its emergency access is for engineers reaching into a customer's workspace, not a clinical record. Halcyon's break-the-glass lets a clinician open a patient chart outside their normal care relationship [1].

**Main differences**

| | Halcyon (Meridian EHR) | Northwind (customer workspaces) |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | Patient care needs it: an unscheduled walk-in, covering a colleague, or an escalation [1] | An open support case or declared incident. Curiosity or speed is not enough [3] |
| Approval | None in the moment; patient care comes first. Manager is asked to confirm if the reason is unclear [1] | A second support or on-call engineer must approve in Teleport. You can't approve your own request or one on the same case [3] |
| Justification | Pick a reason (Emergency care, Coverage, or Other) and write a short explanation [1] | Must reference the case or incident ID [3] |
| Duration | Until end of shift, up to 12 hours [1] | 2 hours, deliberately shorter than the 8-hour standard production session [3] |
| Write access | Not addressed in the source | Read-only by default; write access needs the customer's written consent in the case first [3] |
| Review | Every event logged and reviewed by the Privacy Officer's team within 2 business days [1] | Sessions recorded and kept one year; customer admins emailed within 24 hours; security samples sessions weekly and reviews every write session [3] |
| Misuse | A privacy incident, possibly leading to sanctions up to termination [1] | Prohibited uses include exporting payloads, sharing sessions, and accessing workspaces of people you know [3] |

**Where they're similar:** both prohibit personal use, such as looking up family, coworkers, or yourself [1][3], and both rely on logging and after-the-fact review.

Halcyon's approach favors speed at the point of care, with review afterward. Northwind's requires a peer to approve before access is granted and limits both time and write permissions.

**Short answer: No for patient data at Halcyon, and no for Restricted data at Northwind. The sources don't clearly settle Confidential data at either company.**

**Northwind Labs**
- Restricted data (customer event payloads, credentials, encryption keys) never leaves production and is never allowed in tickets or Slack [1]. Emergency-access guidance repeats this: use field names and counts instead of pasting payloads [3].
- Confidential data (financials, contracts, employee data) is "shared on a need-to-know basis" [1]. The policy doesn't say whether that can happen in Slack.
- Northwind's security policy allows exceptions only with written approval from the Head of Security, and they expire after 90 days [1]. I found no Slack-specific exception process, and nothing that approves Restricted data in Slack.

**Halcyon Health**
- PHI is never allowed in Slack. The systems inventory lists Slack as "Never, including DMs" [2], and the HIPAA policy says the same [7].
- I found no exception or sanctioned-workspace process for PHI in Slack.
- The sources don't cover non-PHI sensitive data (such as employee or financial data) in Slack. The only Slack-related rules I found concern PHI.

**What's missing**
- Whether Northwind Confidential data (financials, contracts, employee data) may be posted in Slack.
- Any Slack-specific exception path at Northwind.
- Any Halcyon rule for non-PHI sensitive data in Slack.

For these gaps, check with Northwind's Security team (`#security-help`) and Halcyon's Privacy Officer and HIPAA Security Officer.

You need sign-off from two people: the Platform change approver and the Head of Security (or the security on-call delegate).

- **Platform change approver: Oluwaseun Adeyemi**, with Kofi Mensah as delegate. Driftwood, the archive that holds these events, is owned by PLAT [7][6]. Lifecycle rules are a normal change, so the owning team's approver signs off [1][2].
- **Head of Security: Tomasz Wierzbicki**, or the security on-call delegate. Driftwood is marked Restricted in the service catalog [7], and normal changes to Restricted services also need Security sign-off [1]. The team directory lists Tomasz as the SEC change approver with security on-call as delegate [6].

Other requirements:

- **ADR:** Any change that alters how long customer data is kept needs an ADR, linked from the PR [1].
- **Customer notice:** Shortening retention requires 30 days' notice from the account team for Enterprise contracts that reference a retention period [1]. You didn't say whether this change shortens or lengthens retention, so I can't tell whether this applies.
- **Longer retention:** Enterprise customers can contract for up to 730 days of archive retention, with security team approval [2].
- **Mechanics:** Add the `change:normal` label to the PR, fill in the risk and rollback sections, and request the approvers as CODEOWNERS reviewers. Approvals expire after 7 days [1].
- **Freezes:** Normal changes are blocked from December 18, 2026 to January 4, 2027. Today is October 31, so that doesn't affect you now [1].

What the sources don't cover: they don't say who the Driftwood-specific lifecycle rule owner is beyond PLAT, or whether any per-workspace overrides need separate approval.

**Short answer:** Escalate to Meridian Clinical Systems. Their P1 response time is 15 minutes, and they are staffed 24/7 [1]. Wren is the Meridian EHR upgrade to release 2027.1 [3], and the cutover is planned for Saturday, February 6, 2027, starting at 22:00 Eastern with 6 hours of planned downtime [2].

**Meridian (EHR), for Wren:**
- P1 response: 15 minutes. P2: 2 hours. Support hours: 24/7 [1].
- The escalation matrix says that for any scheduled Meridian EHR upgrade, Meridian staffs a live bridge line with its own engineers for the whole cutover window, in addition to 24/7 support [1].

**Gaps in the knowledge base:**
- **Bridge line for Wren:** The matrix describes the bridge line for "any scheduled Meridian EHR upgrade" [1], and the register describes Wren as a Meridian EHR upgrade [3]. None of the sources explicitly confirm that the bridge line is booked for Wren's February 6 window.
- **Cutover window:** The February 6 window comes from the October 28 CSCAB minutes [2]. The cutover must finish by 04:00 Sunday so Harbor Point's clinic can open at 10:00 [2]. I found no source that confirms the bridge line covers exactly that window.
- **Escalation during cutover:** The only documented fallback is that if a vendor misses its P1 response, the Service Desk escalates to the vendor's account manager and tells the owning team's steward. Two missed P1 responses in a quarter are reported to the HIPAA Security Officer [1]. I found no cutover-specific escalation path.

**If the problem is in Switchyard or the lab feed:**
- Switchyard is a built-in system with no outside vendor. The Service Desk pages the owning team directly, using the same P1–P3 priorities [1]. The matrix does not name the owning team for Switchyard.
- Results from reference labs come in through Bayline's HL7 feed into Switchyard. Bayline's P1 response is 30 minutes, and its interface desk is staffed 24/7 [1].
- Wren's Switchyard interfaces to all reference labs must be retested by January 15, 2027 [2][3].

**Recommendation:** Before the cutover, confirm with the Wren project lead (Grace Oyelaran) [3] that Meridian's bridge line is contracted for the February 6 window, and confirm who the Switchyard owning team is for on-call paging.

Yes. At Halcyon, every new clinical hire is paired with a preceptor for 90 days, which is the closest equivalent to Northwind's onboarding buddy [1]. The preceptor works with you through these stages:

- **Check-ins:** weekly for the first month, then every other week [1].
- **Competency sign-off:** your preceptor signs off on your competency checklist at 30, 60 and 90 days [1].
- **First week:** you shadow at your home clinic with your preceptor on days 4–5, after HIPAA training and EHR training [1].

**Halcyon patient incidents:** file them in **SafeReport**, the patient safety event reporting system owned by Quality & Patient Safety (QPS) [2][20]. The people who must file are anyone involved in or who witnessed the event, and reporting is never optional and never punished [2].

**Who does what, in order** [2]:
1. Make the patient safe. Follow the clinical escalation protocol and call 911 if needed [2][16].
2. Tell the charge nurse on shift. In clinics without one, tell the clinic manager. The charge nurse coordinates the immediate response [2].
3. For a sentinel event, the charge nurse notifies the on-call medical director within 1 hour [2].
4. Anyone involved or who witnessed the event files in SafeReport [2].
5. The attending clinician discloses the event to the patient or family, with the charge nurse or medical director present [2].

**Event levels:** Level 1 is a sentinel event, Level 2 an adverse event with harm, Level 3 a no-harm event, and Level 4 a near miss. When unsure, report at the higher level [2]. Every Level 1 and Level 2 event gets a root cause analysis, which QPS charters within 72 hours and which must be completed within 45 calendar days of the event becoming known [2].

**What the sources don't say:**
- **Filing deadline:** No source gives a time limit for the reporter to file in SafeReport. The policy's "Within 24 hours" heading covers the immediate steps above, but it does not clearly set a 24-hour filing deadline. Ask QPS or check the full policy for the exact requirement.
- **1-hour medical director notice:** The policy ties this to sentinel events only [2]. It does not say whether any other event needs that call.
- **Other channels:** No source names a channel other than SafeReport for patient-safety events. The IT Service Desk handles system problems. A system fault that creates a patient-safety risk, such as results not arriving, is a P1 ticket [7]. Software-caused events follow the same policy [2].

Privacy incidents are separate. Report them to the Privacy Officer within 24 hours at privacy@halcyon.example or via the compliance hotline [1].

**Northwind production incidents:** Run `/incident declare` in Slack. It opens a channel, starts the timeline, and pages the incident commander rotation [9][12]. For a SEV-1, the IC must be assigned within 15 minutes and the first status page update goes out within 20 minutes [9][12]. Every SEV-1 and SEV-2 gets a blameless postmortem within five business days of resolution [12].

Halcyon's policy says PHI must never go into AI tools that aren't on its approved list. For a new tool that will handle PHI, staff email the Privacy Officer and the HIPAA Security Officer, and the tool needs:

2. A signed business associate agreement with the vendor.
3. An entry in the clinical and business systems inventory.
4. For clinical use, a clinical safety review by the CMIO [1].

labels.text: Halcyon's requirements apply to Halcyon staff, not Northwind.
The knowledge base has no description of the #vendor-review process or how long it takes, so I can't tell you Northwind's turnaround.
Halcyon: what's needed before staff use an AI tool with PHI
Halcyon's policy says PHI must never go into AI tools that aren't on its approved list.
For a new tool that will handle PHI, staff email the Privacy Officer and the HIPAA Security Officer, and the tool needs
A security risk assessment.
A signed business associate agreement with the vendor.
An entry in the clinical and business systems inventory.
For clinical use, a clinical safety review by the CMIO.
Halcyon says the typical turnaround is 6–10 weeks, mostly waiting on the BAA.
Halcyon also treats "de-identified" data as PHI unless it has been properly de-identified, since removing a name isn't enough.
Northwind: what the knowledge base says
Northwind's expense policy says that any software subscription over $50 per month, or anything that will process customer data, must go through the security review in #vendor-review first.
That is the only detail I found.
The knowledge base doesn't include the review's steps, owners, required documents, or timeline.
For those, ask the Security team directly or check whether there is a #vendor-review pinned guide.

rows.answer:
Halcyon's equivalent is the **system steward** for the owning team. For the Halcyon app, that is Felix Brandt, in Digital Health Engineering, Patient Engagement (DHE-PE) [8][15]. The Halcyon app is listed under DHE-PE in the systems inventory, and it holds intake forms and insurance card images, and handles bill pay [15].

**Is his OK enough on its own?** Probably yes, but the sources don't settle it.

- Halcyon's policy calls **cosmetic changes** minor. Minor changes need **steward approval only** [8].
- Significant changes need three things: steward approval, clinical safety sign-off from the CMIO (Dr. Anjali Rao, or delegate Dr. Benedict Osei), and CSCAB review [8]. Significant changes cover patient-facing automation, "the patient app's clinical content," medication information, orders, results routing, and CDS rules [8].
- The sources don't say whether bill-pay screens count as "clinical content." I found no definition of that term, and nothing that places bill pay in or out of it [8][15].

So a purely cosmetic change to the bill-pay screen should be minor and need only Felix Brandt's approval, provided it doesn't touch anything clinical. Confirm that with the CMIO's office or Felix before you ship, since the policy doesn't spell it out. If the change touches anything beyond appearance, such as the content, routing or messages shown to patients, treat it as significant.

Other points:
- Halcyon's change control is run through CSCAB, which meets Wednesdays at 14:00 Eastern [8]. Changes are tracked as CHG numbers [9].
- Northwind's equivalent is different. Its normal production changes need the owning team's change approver, plus Head of Security sign-off for Restricted services [1][4]. Halcyon's model has no separate approver step for minor changes beyond the steward.
